posts:
A decision and an action item serve different purposes in meeting minutes.

The decision records what the group agreed to. The action item identifies what still needs to happen, who is responsible, and when it's expected.

Keeping those details separate makes follow-up easier for volunteer boards and committees.

Try organizing your next meeting with Community Minutes: https://communityminutes.garrettsdevdesk.com

Write meeting minutes for someone who might read them six months from now.

By then, the conversation will have faded from memory. The record should still explain the important decisions, assigned responsibilities, and unfinished business without requiring someone to reconstruct the entire meeting.

What's the most frustrating thing you've encountered when trying to understand old meeting minutes?
